claims.text: The AlCoCrFeNi eutectic alloy initially has a dual-phase lamellar microstructure that exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility during room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Cryogenic HPT or other severe plastic deformation will induce extreme grain refinement and nanotwinning.
The treatment will replace the original lamellar structure with a patterned ultrafine-grained, coherent-nanotwinned structure.
Successful processing can occur between 77 K and 293 K.
Successful processing requires hydrostatic pressure above approximately 5 GPa or an equivalent HPT shear stress.
Successful processing requires more than 100% equivalent plastic strain.
Coherent nanotwin boundaries impede dislocation pile-up while still permitting dislocation transmission.
Cryogenic temperature and high strain rate suppress cross-slip and promote planar dislocation glide.
Planar glide under the proposed processing conditions leads to the formation of dense nanotwins.
Coherent nanotwin boundaries arrest propagation of cracks originating at the original phase interfaces.
Nanotwinning supplies sustained TWIP strain hardening and can mitigate the strength-ductility trade-off.
The treated alloy will change from brittle lamellar failure to ductile failure.
The treated alloy will achieve uniform elongation above 20% together with increased yield strength.
The treatment will preserve the original chemical composition.
Conventional HIP or standard annealing will cause grain growth or retain the lamellar structure without producing enough nanotwins to arrest cracking.
Amorphization or excessive phase decomposition, including sigma-phase formation, would degrade ductility.
The deformation temperature must be low enough to stabilize the FCC phase and favor twinning over slip alone.
The hypothesis is falsified if HPT does not increase nanotwin density relative to HIP or does not produce simultaneous strength and ductility gains under the stated thresholds.
